$comment: Generated by 'make generate-error-codes' from the fault registry. Do not edit: change the registration in Go and regenerate.

codes.summary: The caller may not perform that action on that object
codes.action: Ask an administrator for a grant on the device or on a group that contains it.

codes.summary: An account already holds that username
codes.action: Choose another username, or reset the password on the account that holds this one.

codes.summary: The pairing is no longer waiting for a decision
codes.action: Somebody has already approved or denied it, or it expired. The app asks for a new one.

codes.summary: The person denied the pairing
codes.action: Stop polling. Ask for a new pairing if the person changes their mind. This is access_denied in RFC 8628.

codes.summary: The pairing expired before it was approved
codes.action: Ask for a new pairing and show its code to the person again. This is expired_token in RFC 8628.

codes.summary: Too many pairings are waiting
codes.action: Wait for the pairings already asked for to be answered or to expire, then ask again.

codes.summary: No waiting pairing has that code
codes.action: Check the code the app shows. A pairing waits ten minutes, and the app asks for a new one after that.

codes.summary: Nobody has approved the pairing yet
codes.action: Poll again after the interval. This is authorization_pending in RFC 8628.

codes.summary: The approval names a scope the app did not ask for
codes.action: Approve the scopes the app asked for, or fewer of them.

codes.summary: The app polls faster than it was told to
codes.action: Wait five seconds longer between polls from now on. This is slow_down in RFC 8628.

codes.summary: No pairing answers to that code
codes.action: A code works once. Ask for a new pairing. This is invalid_grant in RFC 8628.

codes.summary: The token was issued for another audience
codes.action: Request a token for the audience this server is configured for, or point the client at the server the token was issued for.

codes.summary: The token has expired or is not valid yet
codes.action: Renew the token at the issuer and retry with the one it returns.

codes.summary: The token names an issuer this server does not accept
codes.action: Present a token from the issuer this server is configured for. The operator sets it on the identity resource.

codes.summary: The issuer's signing keys could not be fetched, so the token cannot be checked
codes.action: Retry after a moment. If it persists, the operator checks that this server reaches the issuer's key set URL.

codes.summary: The token's signature does not verify against the issuer's published keys
codes.action: Sign in at the issuer again and present the token it returns. A token this server accepts is RS256 and signed with a key the issuer publishes.

codes.summary: The token verified, and its subject is not paired to a principal on this server
codes.action: Ask an administrator to pair the subject at POST /api/v1/auth/pairings with the person or service account it should act as, then retry.

codes.summary: The requested expiry has already passed
codes.action: Send an expires_at in the future, or omit it to take the default lifetime.

codes.summary: An api credential cannot be minted for that subject on this server
codes.action: Mint it for a person or a service account, on a deployment that has a login configured.

codes.summary: No api credential has that id
codes.action: List your credentials and use an id from the listing. A revoked credential is gone and needs no second revocation.

codes.summary: The extension may not declare a permission on that object
codes.action: Declare on a resource kind this extension contributes, which is resource_kind:<namespace>/<name>. A permission declared on a core object type is held by every administrator of every object of that type.

codes.summary: The declared permission cannot be granted that way
codes.action: Grant a declared permission on a device whose kind an installed adapter declared it for. An org, a group and a device group span device kinds, a retired name is never reused, and a condition may not qualify a read action.

codes.summary: That identifier already names a device of another kind
codes.action: Give the device an identifier no other device uses. The directory is one identifier space, so a camera registered over a printer of the same identifier would carry that printer's grants.

codes.summary: The authorization graph could not be read
codes.action: Nothing the caller can do. Quote the trace id when reporting it.

codes.summary: The device name is empty or too long
codes.action: Give the device a name of at most 256 bytes.

codes.summary: The identifier is not a DNS-1123 label
codes.action: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63 bytes, starting and ending with an alphanumeric.

codes.summary: The scope is not one this server knows
codes.action: Name at least one of the scopes read, operate and administer.

codes.summary: The authorization graph holds a tuple outside the vocabulary
codes.action: Nothing the caller can do. Quote the trace id when reporting it.

codes.summary: The relation does not accept that kind of subject
codes.action: Grant to a subject shape the relation accepts. A service account cannot hold an org role or a group membership.

codes.summary: The last account on this server cannot be removed
codes.action: Create another account and grant it what this one holds, then remove this one.

codes.summary: The last administrator cannot give the admin role away
codes.action: Give another account the admin role first, then change this one. A server with no administrator has nobody who can add people or change what they may do.

codes.summary: Too many login attempts are waiting from this address
codes.action: Wait for the time Retry-After gives in seconds, then log in again. Attempts from one address are checked one after another.

codes.summary: The username or password is wrong
codes.action: Type the username and the password again. An administrator sets a new password for an account whose password nobody has.

codes.summary: The permissions epoch row is missing
codes.action: Nothing the caller can do. Quote the trace id when reporting it.

codes.summary: This app opened too many page sessions from this address
codes.action: Wait ten minutes, then open the page again.

codes.summary: Only an app pairing credential opens a page session
codes.action: Send the credential an app collected through the app pairing as Authorization: Bearer. A session, a credential a person minted and a page session open none, and a cookie is never read here.

codes.summary: That subject is already paired to a principal on this server
codes.action: Unpair it at DELETE /api/v1/auth/pairings/{provider}/{subject} first, then pair it again.

codes.summary: This operation takes a sign-in as a person
codes.action: Sign in as a person, with your password or with a Prusa Account paired to your account, and repeat the request. An api credential cannot do this, and neither can a Prusa Account token paired to a service account.

codes.summary: First-run setup has already completed on this server
codes.action: Sign in as an existing user. Setup cannot be reopened over the API.

codes.summary: Too many wrong setup codes were sent
codes.action: Wait for the time the message names, then send the code again. Retry-After gives the same wait in seconds. A restart of the server clears the count and prints a new code.

codes.summary: The setup code is missing or wrong
codes.action: Send the setup code in the code field. The server prints it in its log when it starts: read it with docker logs for a container or journalctl for a service. A restart prints a new code, and an install that sets core.auth.setup_code takes that value.

codes.summary: This server has not been set up yet
codes.action: Open this server in a browser and finish the first run with the setup code from its log, or POST /api/v1/setup with that code and the mode this deployment should serve. Every other path answers this until one is recorded.

codes.summary: The credential is not one this server accepts
codes.action: Authenticate again and retry with the token that returns. Quote the trace id if a fresh token is refused too.

codes.summary: The authorization graph has no such action
codes.action: Check one of the actions the vocabulary defines. Roles are not checkable.

codes.summary: The type does not have that relation
codes.action: Use a relation the vocabulary defines on this type.

codes.summary: The authorization graph has no such type
codes.action: Use one of the types the vocabulary defines. It is closed and cannot be extended at runtime.

codes.summary: Actions are not defined on that object type
codes.action: Check an action on a device. Other object types carry structure and grants, not actions.

codes.summary: The server is decompressing files of the web app for as many other clients as it allows
codes.action: Wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After and ask again, or send Accept-Encoding: gzip to get the file at once. A browser always sends it, so a browser never gets this answer.

codes.summary: The link did not answer this request inside the budget, or answered something this server will not read
codes.action: Read the instance at /api/v1/resources to see where it stands, and read its log for what the link said. A link that runs as a module is restarted by switching the instance off and on again.

codes.summary: This server could not write the release into its modules directory
codes.action: Check that core.modules names a directory this server can write, such as one on a volume rather than beside a read-only configuration file, then install again.

codes.summary: The disk that holds the module's data has no room for the request body
codes.action: Send a smaller body, or ask the operator to free space on the server's disk and then send it again.

codes.summary: The module is receiving as many large bodies at once as the server allows it
codes.action: Wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After and send the body again.

codes.summary: The resource is failing and its circuit breaker is open
codes.action: Retry after the breaker's cooldown, and check the resource for the underlying failure.

codes.summary: The instance requires a contract whose provider requires it back, so nothing in the ring could start
codes.action: Remove one requirement in the ring named here, or take one of its instances out of the configuration.

codes.summary: The module requires a contract that no serving module provides, so it was not started
codes.action: Install and switch on a module that provides the contract named here, or start the one that does. This instance starts by itself once one is serving.

codes.summary: The module requires something this build of the server does not offer, so it was not started
codes.action: Run a build of the server that serves the capability or falls in the core range named here, or install a release of the module built for this server.

codes.summary: The module cannot work without a request header this server did not grant it, so it was not started
codes.action: Grant the header named here in service.request_headers of the instance, or install the module again with approve.

codes.summary: The artefact that answered is not the module the install recorded, so it was not run
codes.action: Reinstall the module from the release you want, so the declaration and the artefact name the same module, release and plugin contract.

codes.summary: The module ships a module.yaml the host will not read, so nothing of it was served
codes.action: Fix the manifest in the module's bundle, record the digest of the bundle as it is now, and restart the instance.

codes.summary: The module's data directory was made for another module that was installed under the same name, so the module was not started
codes.action: Remove the folder the error names, or move it away if its data is still needed, then restart the instance.

codes.summary: The module was granted a data directory and the server could not create it, so the module was not started
codes.action: Give the server write access to the directory beside its modules directory, or move core.modules to a disk it can write, then restart the instance.

codes.summary: Another running instance already serves the module's service.mount, so the instance was not started
codes.action: Give this instance a different prefix and reload the configuration, or free the prefix by removing or disabling the instance holding it and then switch this instance off and on so it starts again.

codes.summary: The module's service.mount is not a root prefix this server can route, so the instance was not started
codes.action: Write an absolute path with no trailing slash, no dot segment and no character a path segment cannot carry, such as /graphql or /app/api, then reload the configuration.

codes.summary: The module's service.mount is a path this server serves itself, so the instance was not started
codes.action: Choose a prefix outside /api, the OpenAPI document, the reference, /metrics, /dev and every path a connector mounted, then reload the configuration.

codes.summary: The resource is not serving requests
codes.action: Check the resource state and retry once it is ready.

codes.summary: The resource panicked and was taken out of service
codes.action: Nothing the caller can do. Quote the trace id when reporting it.

codes.summary: The artefact is not the bytes its recorded checksum covers, so it was not launched or served
codes.action: Reinstall the extension, or record the checksum of the file that is now there.

codes.summary: The extension implements a plugin contract major this host does not serve
codes.action: Install a build of the extension for this host, or run a host that serves the major it needs.

codes.summary: The instance names an artefact that is not where the declaration says, so there is nothing to launch or serve
codes.action: Install the extension where the instance says it is, then restart the instance.

codes.summary: The instance's config block is not what the module reads, so the module was not started
codes.action: Read the keys the module declares at GET /api/v1/resources, fix the config block of this instance, and reload the configuration.

codes.summary: The instance carries a config block and the module answers no plugin.configure, so it was not started
codes.action: Remove the config block from this instance, or install a release of the module that reads settings.

codes.summary: The module serves HTTP routes and ships no OpenAPI fragment for them, so it was not mounted
codes.action: Attach the module's OpenAPI 3.1 fragment to its plugin.info answer with routesapi.Describe, then restart the instance.

codes.summary: The resource is too slow and its queue is full, so the item was dropped
codes.action: Retry. A resource that drops continuously is too slow for its offered load.

codes.summary: The module keeps its data in the record store and no record backend is serving, so it was not started
codes.action: Declare a record backend under resources.db, such as one of type sqlite, or start the one that is declared. This instance starts by itself once one is serving.

codes.summary: The resource failed to start too many times and is no longer being retried
codes.action: Fix the underlying failure, then restart the resource.

codes.summary: The resource did not answer within its budget
codes.action: Retry. A resource that times out repeatedly is unreachable rather than slow.

codes.summary: The instance names a type this build of the server does not have, so it was not started
codes.action: Write one of the types the error lists in the instance's type key, or run a build of the server that has this type, then reload the configuration.

codes.summary: The server failed in a way it does not describe
codes.action: Nothing the caller can do. Quote the trace id when reporting it.

codes.summary: The server returned an error it does not document
codes.action: Nothing the caller can do. Quote the trace id when reporting it.

codes.summary: The printer does not have that capability
codes.action: Send one of the verbs this error carries as verbs, which is the capability set this server resolved for the printer. It is a JSON array of strings and not a joined list, so a key reads back whole. verb_count is how many verbs the printer has: a count above the length of the array means the array is the first 128 and the printer's own capability set is the rest. The set is handed out with an epoch, and the epoch moves whenever the printer reconnects, so a set kept from an earlier epoch describes a printer that is no longer there: read it again rather than caching it across a reconnect.

codes.summary: The printer took the command and could not carry it out
codes.action: Read the machine reason this carries, which is the printer's own word for what went wrong, then read the printer's state. The printer accepted the command and failed part way through it, so it may have changed something: this is not resent for you and sending it again is a second attempt rather than a first.

codes.summary: The printer took the command, could not carry it out, and gave no reason for it
codes.action: Read the printer's state and the job it is running, because the failure itself says nothing more than that it happened. The printer accepted the command and did not finish it, so it may have changed something: sending it again is a second attempt rather than a first.

codes.summary: The printer is already holding as many commands as it takes
codes.action: Wait for the printer to answer what it is holding and send this command again. Nothing was sent, so the command was not carried out twice. A printer that is away holds its queue until it comes back, so a queue that stays full is a printer that is not answering.

codes.summary: The printer refused the command
codes.action: Read the machine reason this refusal carries, which is the printer's own word for why. Whether sending it again can work depends on that word and not on the refusal: a file that is already there is answered by printing it, and a printer busy with a job is answered by waiting. Nothing was carried out, so nothing was carried out twice.

codes.summary: The printer is busy with another command and refused this one
codes.action: The printer did not carry the command out because it is still working on a command it received earlier. Wait for that command to finish and send this one again. If it keeps refusing, read the printer's state and the job it is running.

codes.summary: The printer refused the command
codes.action: Check what the printer is doing and send it again. A printer refuses a command its current state does not allow.

codes.summary: The printer lost its connection before it answered the command
codes.action: The command reached the printer, so it may have been carried out. Read the printer's state when it connects again and decide from that, rather than sending the command a second time. This server does not resend it for you.

codes.summary: The printer runs this server, so it cannot be removed from it
codes.action: Keep the printer. Its record says resident: true. To stop using this server, switch it off on the printer.

codes.summary: The printer refused that change to its storage
codes.action: Read the machine reason this error carries. A create refused because the name is taken is answered by choosing another; a delete refused because the path names nothing is answered by listing the directory first.

codes.summary: A file of that name is already on the printer
codes.action: Ask the person whether to replace the file on the printer. If they agree, send the same request again with replace set to true, which deletes the printer's file first. Otherwise send the file under another name.

codes.summary: The printer did not say the firmware file's short name, so the server did not send the flash
codes.action: Nothing was flashed. Send the flash again once the printer answers. The message says what the printer did instead of answering.

codes.summary: This server never sends that gcode word
codes.action: Use the verb that covers what the code does. Files are written and deleted through the file capabilities, which check the path, and firmware is not updated through this API at all. No grant lifts this refusal.

codes.summary: No print of that id is held
codes.action: Read the print id from a printer's jobs or its print history. A print on a printer you cannot see reads the same as one that never existed.

codes.summary: The printer refused to report what is at that path
codes.action: Read the machine reason this error carries, which is the printer's own word for why. For a path that names nothing, list the directory above it. For a printer that takes no command in its state, clear that state at the machine and ask again.

codes.summary: The printer did not finish reading the folder
codes.action: Ask for the folder again once the printer is connected. An MK4S takes 12 to 15 s to list a USB root of about 300 files, and a read still running after two minutes is stopped.

codes.summary: No printer is registered with that id
codes.action: Read the id from the printer list. An id that was removed is not reissued, so a stored one can go stale.

codes.summary: This server pairs only with a printer on the local network
codes.action: Type the address the printer shows on its network screen: a private address such as 192.168.1.20, or a name that resolves to one.

codes.summary: The printer is printing or shows another dialog, so it cannot ask about pairing
codes.action: Wait until the printer is idle and its screen shows no dialog, then try again.

codes.summary: Pairing is off on the printer until it restarts
codes.action: A person cancelled two pairing questions in a row. Restart the printer to pair again, or add it with a settings file instead.

codes.summary: This server already has a pairing open with that printer, or too many open at once
codes.action: Cancel the open pairing or wait a minute for it to end, then try again.

codes.summary: The printer takes no pairing request for a while
codes.action: Wait for the time Retry-After gives in seconds. A printer locks pairing for five minutes after a cancel, a question nobody answered, or three requests in five minutes.

codes.summary: The printer already shows a pairing question
codes.action: Answer or cancel the question on the printer, or wait a minute for it to close, then try again.

codes.summary: The printer refused the pairing request
codes.action: The detail says which value the printer refused. A server address longer than the printer stores is the usual cause: use the IP address instead of a long name.

codes.summary: The printer cannot use the server address in the request
codes.action: Give an address the printer reaches this server at: not localhost, at most 35 characters, and a port between 1 and 65535.

codes.summary: This server got no answer from the printer
codes.action: Check the printer's address on its network screen, and that the printer and this server are on the same network.

codes.summary: The printer's firmware cannot pair
codes.action: Update the printer's firmware, or add the printer with a settings file on a USB drive.

codes.summary: The path leaves the storage it names
codes.action: Send a path relative to the storage, with no .. segment. A path is checked as it reaches the device, so prefixing a storage onto a path that climbs does not make it legal.

codes.summary: The preset names printer models and this printer is not one of them
codes.action: Run a preset that names this printer's model, or one that names no model at all. Gcode that is safe on one model is not safe on another, so nothing was sent.

codes.summary: The printer changed while the command was waiting, so it was not sent
codes.action: Read the printer's capability set again and send the command against it. The command was composed for the firmware the printer had before, the printer came back reporting another one, and nothing was sent to the machine.

codes.summary: The printer is a read-only mirror of one owned by another server
codes.action: Send the command to the server that owns the printer. State and events for it stay readable here.

codes.summary: The printer's session has ended
codes.action: Wait for the printer to connect again. Its last state stays readable while it is away.

codes.summary: The printer is already fetching a file
codes.action: Wait for the transfer in flight to finish, or stop it, then send this one. A printer fetches one file at a time and starting a second would abandon the first.

codes.summary: The transfer did not finish
codes.action: Send the file again. A transfer that stops part way leaves nothing usable on the printer, and the event this reports is the printer's own word for how it ended.

codes.summary: No transfer of that id is running
codes.action: Read the transfer id from the printer's transfer list. A transfer that has already ended cannot be stopped, and reads the same as one that never existed.

codes.summary: The printer reported the transfer finished and the file is not on its storage
codes.action: Send the file under a name that no entry in that directory already shares. A FAT storage shortens every long name to an 8.3 spelling, and two long names that shorten to the same one are one entry: the second file has nowhere to land. Sending the same name again lands in the same place.

codes.summary: The printer would not take the file
codes.action: Read the machine reason this error carries. A printer refuses a transfer its storage or its current state does not allow, so the answer depends on which: make room, remove the file that is already there, or wait for the printer to finish what it is doing.

codes.summary: The file is longer than a transfer to this printer can describe
codes.action: Send a file below limit_bytes. The length travels to the printer as an unsigned 32-bit count of bytes, so 4 GiB is the first size that has no spelling on the wire.

codes.summary: The device's state does not allow that verb
codes.action: Send the verb again once the device reports a state that allows it. The state named here is the one the refusal was decided on, so a device that has changed state since answers differently.

codes.summary: This build has no such capability verb
codes.action: Send a verb from the capability vocabulary at /api/v1/vocabularies/capabilities, and one the device's own kind declares: the verb table has a row per kind, so a verb another kind carries does not exist for this one, and kind says which kind the device is. A spelling that differs from a verb only in case or in the missing core.command. prefix is answered with suggested_verb, which is this API's name for it. The shipping server's SET_NOZZLE_TEMPERATURE is core.command.set_nozzle_temperature here.

codes.summary: The Beta Portal suspended the tester's access to the product
codes.action: The pairing stays. Ask the product team to restore the access of the tester this server is paired as; updates work again without pairing anew.

codes.summary: This server is already paired with the Beta Portal
codes.action: Disconnect the current pairing first if you want to pair this server with another account.

codes.summary: The Beta Portal refused the request because this server's clock is wrong
codes.action: Set the date and time of the machine this server runs on, or turn on time synchronisation (NTP), then try again.

codes.summary: The update server refused this server because it is not paired with the Beta Portal
codes.action: Pair this server in Settings, Updates. A pairing removed or revoked in the portal has to be made again.

codes.summary: The Beta Portal asked this server to wait before pairing again
codes.action: Wait for the number of seconds the message names, then start pairing again. Retry-After gives the same wait.

codes.summary: The local pairing was cleared but remote revocation was not confirmed
codes.action: This server no longer uses the pairing. The Beta Portal could not be reached to revoke the old token, so remove this device in the portal when it is available.

codes.summary: The Beta Portal did not answer the pairing request
codes.action: Try again in a moment. If it keeps failing, check that core.upgrade.server is right and that this server can reach it.

codes.summary: The camera did not answer, so there is no picture to serve
codes.action: Try again in a moment. If it keeps failing, check that the camera is powered on and that this server reaches the address the instance declares.

codes.summary: This server already holds as many dashboards as it keeps
codes.action: Delete a dashboard nobody uses, then make the new one. The server keeps at most limit_dashboards dashboards.

codes.summary: Somebody saved this dashboard after you read it
codes.action: Read the dashboard again, make the change against the revision it answers, and send it again. The server refuses the change rather than writing over the other person's.

codes.summary: There is no dashboard with this id that you may see
codes.action: Open the list of dashboards and pick one from it. A deleted dashboard's id is never given to another one, so an old link does not open a different dashboard.

codes.summary: This deployment keeps no history of the kind the request asks for
codes.action: Declare a history instance under resources.history in the server's configuration. A provider that is serving answers this on the half of the contract it does not serve, and one that is restarting reads the same as one never declared. Events already published are gone: a provider stores what it sees from the moment it is attached.

codes.summary: The history provider will not answer a query in this shape
codes.action: Ask for a window the provider still keeps, or the coarsest step it names. A provider refuses rather than approximating, because a short page of raw samples reads exactly like a printer that was switched off.

codes.summary: Two history instances both answer this query, and the server will not guess
codes.action: Write a reads: list on each of the two declarations, so that one of them names this verb and the other does not. An instance with no reads: list claims every verb its capabilities carry, so a list on one of the two leaves the other claiming this verb as well.

codes.summary: This build installs no module over HTTP
codes.action: Install the module with the `module add` command against this server's configuration file, and restart the core. A build that serves the install paths is one started from a configuration file it may write an overlay beside.

codes.summary: The marketplace is switched off on this server
codes.action: Switch the marketplace on again in the Extensions settings, or install the release from a path or an address in from. Modules already installed from it keep running.

codes.summary: The marketplace did not answer, so this server cannot say what it offers
codes.action: Try again in a moment. If it keeps failing, check that core.marketplace.url is right and that this server reaches it, or install the release from a path or an address in from.

codes.summary: This server installs no module and runs none it installed
codes.action: The operator set core.modules_enabled to false in the configuration file, so this server installs no module and starts none it installed. Modules declared in that file still run, and an installed module can still be removed. To install or start modules, set core.modules_enabled to true, or delete the line, and restart the server.

codes.summary: This server could not make the module's database on its Postgres server
codes.action: Nothing was installed. reason says what the database server answered. Give the role in persistence.postgres.module_admin_dsn the rights CREATEDB and CREATEROLE, or drop a role or a database of the name found that belongs to something else. Or install with the database mode sqlite, or postgres with a dsn.

codes.summary: This server could not drop a database a module left behind
codes.action: Nothing of that database was dropped, and it is still listed. reason says what the database server answered. A role or a database of the name found whose comment or owner names another module is never dropped: drop it by hand if it is yours, then purge with forget. Otherwise give the role in persistence.postgres.module_admin_dsn the right to drop what it made, and purge again.

codes.summary: No release of a module is in the range of every module that needs it
codes.action: requires names who needs what. Update the module whose range is out of date, or install a release of the new module that fits the modules already installed.

codes.summary: The module needs another module that is not installed, is switched off, or has a release out of range
codes.action: requires names each module it needs, the range, and what this server has. Install, switch on or update that module, then try again.

codes.summary: A module the install needs is in no index this server reads
codes.action: requires names each missing module and its range. Install it from a release file first, add it to the index in the modules directory or to core.modules_local, or switch the marketplace on.

codes.summary: This server could not download the release
codes.action: Try again in a moment. If it keeps failing, the release's address is not one this server downloads from: it answered with an error, or it leads to this machine or the local network. Install the release from a path on this server instead.

codes.summary: The module's files could not be deleted, so it is still installed
codes.action: Send the same request again in a moment. If it keeps failing, something on this server is holding a file under the named path open. Close it, or delete the directory by hand, and the declaration goes with the next request.

codes.summary: Another enabled module already reads or draws files of the same type
codes.action: conflicts names both modules, what each does with the files and the file types they share. Switch the other module off or remove it, or install a release of this one that names other file types.

codes.summary: modules.lock.json could not be written
codes.action: The detail says whether the change was refused before anything was written or stands without a lock that names it. Make the directory of the lock writable, then try again, or run module update, which writes the lock again. resource names the module.

codes.summary: Another module is installed under the same name
codes.action: Remove the module that holds the name first, or install a release with another name. type is the type declared under the name now, and found is the type of this release.

codes.summary: The modules the install would add are not the ones that were approved
codes.action: The index or the installed modules changed since the plan was read. Read the plan again, approve it, and install again. Nothing was written. found is the plan the server resolved now.

codes.summary: The release asks for more than the operator was shown
codes.action: Nothing was installed. Read the module index again, or install without approve to read what the release asks for, then approve exactly that. source says what the operator was shown, and found lists each request beyond it.

codes.summary: Other installed modules require this module
codes.action: requires names each module that requires this one and its range. Remove or switch off those modules first, or update them to releases that work with the change.

codes.summary: The new release did not start, so the release it replaced runs again
codes.action: Nothing of the update was kept: the files, the declaration and the grants are those of the release named declared, and a database of the module's own is as it was before, because a migration that fails is undone whole. reason says why the new release did not start, such as a migration that failed or a database a newer release migrated. Install a release that fixes it.

codes.summary: This server runs in safe mode, so it runs no module
codes.action: Safe mode starts no module, installed or declared in the configuration file, and installs none. A module can still be removed and its settings changed. Restart the server normally to start modules again.

codes.summary: This deployment keeps no module state, so there is nowhere to read or write a record
codes.action: Declare a db instance under resources.db in the server's configuration. Every module namespace is served from that one backend, and a deployment with none serves no module record at all.

codes.summary: The update is not in a state that allows this step
codes.action: Reload the Updates page to see where the update is now. Another update may be running, or this one may already have finished or rolled back.

codes.summary: The server refused the update or the backup it was given
codes.action: The message names the check that failed, such as the signature, the checksum or the platform. Use a release built and signed for this server.

codes.summary: The update server refused the request because this server asked too often
codes.action: Wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After, then ask again. The server keeps the release list for a few minutes, so reloading the page does not ask the update server again.

codes.summary: Some of the entries in the delete request are still there
codes.action: List the directory and repeat the delete for what remains. The entries that were removed stay removed.

codes.summary: The file extension is not one this storage accepts
codes.action: Upload a file with an allowed extension. The allow-list is per storage and is part of the server configuration.

codes.summary: The storage holds no file of that name
codes.action: List the storage and send a name it reports. The name is relative to the storage root.

codes.summary: The request names a path this storage will not accept
codes.action: Send a path relative to the storage root, with no .. segment and no drive or leading separator.

codes.summary: No storage of that name is serving
codes.action: Read the names from the resource list. A storage that is declared but not ready is not usable yet, and its status says why.

codes.summary: That storage cannot open a file for reading
codes.action: Use a storage whose type serves files. The types this build carries are listed at startup and in the extension reference.

codes.summary: The storage ran out of space while writing the file
codes.action: Free space on this storage or upload to another one, then send the file again. Treat the target path as unusable until it is deleted.

codes.summary: That file carries no picture
codes.action: Show the file without one. A picture comes from the slicer: a .gcode, .bgcode or .3mf file exported with thumbnails enabled has one, and an .stl file never has one.

codes.summary: The storage could not carry that out
codes.action: Read the server log for the reason. The request itself may be fine: this is the code for a failure the server could not attribute to anything the caller sent.

codes.summary: The value is not in the form the argument accepts
codes.action: For a number, send a whole or a fractional number. For a boolean, send true or false. For text, send only the characters allowed_characters names, and no more than limit_characters of them.

codes.summary: The command needs an argument that was not supplied
codes.action: Supply the argument. It has no default, so there is nothing for the server to fall back to.

codes.summary: The printer does not support that value for the argument
codes.action: Choose one of the supported values, which this error carries as a JSON array of strings. It is an array and not a joined list so that a value containing a comma reads back whole.

codes.summary: The argument is outside the range the printer accepts
codes.action: Send a value no further from zero than max, and at or above min. The refusal carries whichever of the two the value broke.

codes.summary: The command does not accept that argument
codes.action: Send only the arguments the capability declares. An argument that used to exist is not silently ignored, because a command carried out with a dropped argument is not the command that was asked for.

codes.summary: The request body is larger than this endpoint accepts
codes.action: Send at most limit_bytes, or use the upload endpoint, which streams instead of buffering.

codes.summary: The dashboard breaks one of the rules a dashboard is held to
codes.action: Correct the member named by location as the reason says, and send the dashboard again.

codes.summary: Another diagnostics bundle is being built
codes.action: Wait for the bundle in progress to finish, then ask again. The server builds one at a time.

codes.summary: The write changes a field that is fixed for the life of the instance
codes.action: Delete the instance and declare a new one. A different implementation cannot inherit the identity of the old one, and the data rows that reference it would follow the wrong type.

codes.summary: The body is not the JPEG image this operation takes
codes.action: Send the frame as image/jpeg, with the encoded image as the whole body. Nothing is converted here, so a camera that cannot encode JPEG cannot use this path.

codes.summary: The payload is not one gcode command
codes.action: Send one command: a G, M or T followed immediately by its number, then its parameters, in printable ASCII and on one line. Several commands are a sequence, not a payload, so split them and send them as separate steps.

codes.summary: The path exists but publishes no operation for that method
codes.action: Use one of the methods the OpenAPI document lists for this path.

codes.summary: The downloaded release is not the one the request or the marketplace names
codes.action: The bytes fetched from the release's address hash to another SHA-256 than the one stated, so this server refused them before unpacking anything. Ask the marketplace for the module again, or check that the address and the digest belong together.

codes.summary: The marketplace offers no such release for this server
codes.action: Read the module index again and install a version a row offers, or name the release's address in from. The marketplace lists only releases built for this server's platform and accepting its version.

codes.summary: A module claims this address and is not serving on it
codes.action: Read the instance at /api/v1/resources to see where it stands. A module that is switched on and whose files are not installed is installed with `prusa-connect module add`; one that is switched off is started by declaring it enabled.

codes.summary: The write carries no precondition, and this resource has another writer
codes.action: Read the resource, then send its ETag back in the named header, quotes included. Send If-None-Match: * to create an instance that must not exist yet.

codes.summary: The caller closed the request before the server answered it
codes.action: Read the resource to see whether the work went through before sending it again: the caller stopped waiting, and work already on its way, such as a command written to a printer, may still have happened.

codes.summary: The request does not match the schema the operation publishes
codes.action: Correct the member named by location and send it again. The schema is in the OpenAPI document at /openapi.json.

codes.summary: The request took longer than the budget this server gives one
codes.action: Read the resource to see whether the work went through before sending it again: the budget ends the wait and not the work. An operator moves the bound at core.api.request_timeout, and the streaming and file routes carry core.api.stream_timeout instead.

codes.summary: No resource instance of that kind carries that name
codes.action: List the kind to see what is configured. A name is unique within its kind and nowhere wider.

codes.summary: The instance is declared and the supervision plane is not running it
codes.action: Read the instance and look at enabled. A disabled instance is started by declaring it enabled, which is a write and takes configure_resource; a kind with nothing to supervise has no instance to restart at all.

codes.summary: The instance is declared in the hand-authored configuration file, which the API does not write
codes.action: Edit the file named by file and reload, or move the instance to the machine-owned overlay first. The API writes the overlay only, so the operator's file keeps its comments.

codes.summary: No operation is published at that path
codes.action: Check the path against the OpenAPI document at /openapi.json.

codes.summary: The value is larger than one module state record may hold
codes.action: Store at most limit_bytes under one key. A document that does not fit is a file and belongs on a storage instance, which streams.

codes.summary: A device is given more tags than this server accepts
codes.action: Send at most limit_tags tags for one device.

codes.summary: A tag contains a character this server does not accept
codes.action: Remove any comma, line break, tab or character that does not show on screen. An accent or a part of an emoji must come right after a letter, a digit or a symbol, and not at the start of a word. The device list uses commas to separate tags.

codes.summary: The same tag is given twice
codes.action: Send each tag once. Two tags are the same tag when they differ only in upper and lower case, or in the invisible characters that join letters or pick how an emoji looks.

codes.summary: A tag has no visible character
codes.action: Remove the empty tag, or type a word or a short phrase into it.

codes.summary: A tag is longer than this server accepts
codes.action: Shorten the tag named by tag to at most limit_characters characters.

codes.summary: This caller already holds as many event streams as the server allows one
codes.action: Close a stream before opening another. One stream carries every origin the caller may observe, so a second is rarely needed; narrow one with the origins parameter instead.

codes.summary: The file is larger than this server accepts
codes.action: Send a file of at most {limit_bytes}. An administrator sets the largest file with core.api.max_upload_size.

codes.summary: The instance changed since the version the write quotes
codes.action: Read the instance again, reapply the change to what it now says, and send the new ETag. Somebody else wrote it, possibly by editing the configuration file directly.
